name: Baby Aarav Sharma
chief_complaint: High fever for 2 days, marked lethargy, poor feeding, rapid breathing
hpi_narrative: Mother reports 18-month-old infant has been unusually quiet and irritable. Refusing fluids since morning. Temp spiked to 39.2°C at home. Noticed retractions when breathing.
clinical_rationale: Severe pediatric tachypnea (RR 48) and tachycardia (HR 168) with SpO2 93% and lethargy indicates high PEWS risk. Rapid decompensation risk requires immediate ESI 2 acute pediatric resuscitation.

name: Ramesh Kumar
chief_complaint: Mild indigestion, feeling unusually exhausted and sweaty for 3 hours
hpi_narrative: 78-year-old diabetic male denies classic chest pain or radiation. Complains of epigastric fullness, mild nausea, and sudden profuse diaphoresis after climbing stairs. Appears pale and clammy.
clinical_rationale: Classic geriatric 'silent/atypical' coronary syndrome presentation. Diabetic neuropathy masks chest pain. Disproportionate diaphoresis and borderline hemodynamics warrant safety-first escalation to ESI 2 for immediate STAT ECG.

name: Walk-in Anonymous Patient
chief_complaint: Acute moderate shortness of breath and wheezing after dust exposure
hpi_narrative: 28-year-old female arrived alone with no prior hospital ID. Reports sudden onset tightness in chest and expiratory wheeze. Speaking in partial sentences.
clinical_rationale: Zero prior baseline data creates initial uncertainty margin. Tachypneic with mild hypoxia (94%) and wheezing. Stable enough for urgent treatment area (ESI 3) with nebulization and close queue monitoring.

name: Sneha Patel
chief_complaint: Severe exacerbation of shortness of breath, purulent sputum, cyanotic lips
hpi_narrative: Known frequent ED attendee with severe COPD. Woke up gasping for air. Using accessory muscles of respiration. Speaking in 1-word gasps.
clinical_rationale: Critical respiratory distress (RR 32, SpO2 87%) on top of documented advanced baseline lung disease. Immediate non-invasive ventilation / emergent intervention required (ESI 2).

name: Kavita Mukherjee
chief_complaint: Acute new confusion, somnolence, shivering, dark foul-smelling urine
hpi_narrative: Daughter brought patient stating mother was oriented yesterday but cannot answer questions today. Note blunted temperature (36.6°C) but marked tachycardia and borderline hypotension.
clinical_rationale: Geriatric blunted febrile response. qSOFA score >= 2 (Altered mental status + SBP <= 100 + RR >= 22) indicates high mortality risk from severe sepsis. Escalated immediately to ESI 2.

name: Marcus Thomas
chief_complaint: Severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain, vomiting, fever
hpi_narrative: 12-year-old male with 14-hour history of periumbilical pain migrating to McBurney's point. Guarding and marked rebound tenderness on palpation. Unable to jump or walk upright.
clinical_rationale: High pain score (9/10), acute peritonitis signs, fever, and tachycardia in pediatric patient indicate high risk of perforation. Requires urgent surgical evaluation and IV hydration (ESI 2).

name: Rajesh Verma
chief_complaint: Crushing substernal chest pressure, radiating to left arm and jaw, profuse cold sweats
hpi_narrative: 52-year-old male clutching chest in triage. Onset 45 mins ago while shoveling. Described as 'elephant sitting on chest'. Severe nausea and impending sense of doom.
clinical_rationale: High-probability active myocardial infarction with severe hemodynamics and maximal pain rating. Immediate resuscitation bed, cardiac monitor, STAT ECG within 5 minutes (ESI 1/2 immediate).

name: Priya Singh
chief_complaint: Clean superficial papercut on right index finger, minor bleeding stopped
hpi_narrative: 24-year-old female sustained a 1cm clean superficial cut at office. Wound is clean, bleeding stopped with direct pressure. Full range of motion, neurovascularly intact.
clinical_rationale: Completely stable vitals, zero resource requirements beyond simple dressing or antiseptic advice. Diverted to Fast-Track / Triage Out to preserve acute ED capacity.

name: Dev Dixit
chief_complaint: Inversion ankle injury playing basketball, localized lateral swelling
hpi_narrative: 34-year-old male twisted left ankle 2 hours ago. Able to bear weight with limp. Moderate edema over anterior talofibular ligament. Skin intact, distal pulses brisk.
clinical_rationale: Stable vitals, single anticipated resource (Ankle X-Ray + splint/wrap). ESI Level 4 sub-acute care.

name: Ananya Banerjee
chief_complaint: Barking seal-like cough, audible inspiratory stridor at rest, tracheal tugging
hpi_narrative: 4-year-old female woke up at 2 AM with severe stridor. Subcostal and suprasternal retractions visible. Agitated, SpO2 dropping to 91% on room air.
clinical_rationale: Inspiratory stridor AT REST in a 4-year-old with oxygen desaturation (91%) represents impending respiratory failure from severe croup/epiglottitis. Immediate ESI 1 resuscitation.

name: Vikram Sethi
chief_complaint: Sudden right-sided arm paralysis, facial droop, slurred speech (onset 35 mins ago)
hpi_narrative: Wife noticed sudden inability to hold coffee cup and garbled speech at 6:45 PM. Last known normal 35 minutes ago. Clear neurological deficit, stroke code window open.
clinical_rationale: Acute focal neurological deficit within 4.5hr thrombolytic window. Immediate STAT non-contrast head CT and Code Stroke activation. ESI 1 emergent routing.

name: Fatima Zaidi
chief_complaint: Severe lower quadrant sharp pelvic pain, 7 weeks pregnant, vaginal spotting, dizzy
hpi_narrative: 31-year-old female positive home pregnancy test 2 weeks ago. Sudden excruciating unilateral pelvic pain and shoulder tip pain. Syncope episode 10 minutes ago.
clinical_rationale: High risk of life-threatening intra-abdominal hemorrhage. Tachycardia (HR 120) with borderline hypotension and syncope in early pregnancy mandates ESI 2 emergent bedside ultrasound.

name: Carlos Mendez
chief_complaint: High spiking fever (39.5°C), rust-colored productive cough, right pleuritic chest pain
hpi_narrative: 48-year-old male with 4 days of progressive fever, shaking chills, and dense right lower lobe crackles on auscultation. SpO2 91% on room air.
clinical_rationale: High fever, tachypnea (RR 26), and hypoxia (91%) meet systemic inflammatory criteria with compromised gas exchange. Assigned ESI 2 for supplemental O2 and IV antibiotics.

name: Anita Roy
chief_complaint: Mechanical fall from bed, hit forehead on nightstand, taking blood thinners
hpi_narrative: 82-year-old on full-dose oral anticoagulation suffered head strike. Mild 2cm hematoma over left temporal area. Glasgow Coma Scale 14 (slightly repetitive speech).
case_type: Geriatric Anticoagulated Head Injury (Intracranial Bleed Risk)
clinical_rationale: High mortality risk from delayed intracranial hemorrhage in elderly patient on direct oral anticoagulants with head trauma. Escalated to ESI 2 for STAT non-contrast Head CT.

name: Rahul Nair
chief_complaint: Mild scratchy throat and runny nose for 1 day, wants prescription
hpi_narrative: 19-year-old student reports mild rhinorrhea and pharyngeal discomfort. No fever, no difficulty swallowing, no shortness of breath. Vitals completely normal.
case_type: Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (Minor Fast Track)
clinical_rationale: Normal physiology, zero urgent interventions required. Routed to outpatient clinic / fast-track.

name: Sunita Joshi
chief_complaint: Severe throbbing unilateral headache with photophobia and nausea for 6 hours
hpi_narrative: 55-year-old female with typical migraine symptoms, unresponsive to home Sumatriptan. Denies fever, neck stiffness, or sudden 'thunderclap' onset. Pupils equal and reactive.
clinical_rationale: High pain score requiring multiple IV abortive medications (antiemetic, NSAID, fluids) and dark quiet observation. ESI 3.

name: David Kim
chief_complaint: Acute excruciating right flank pain radiating to groin, gross hematuria, severe restlessness
hpi_narrative: 42-year-old male pacing the triage floor unable to find comfortable position. Onset 2 hours ago. 10/10 colicky pain. Nausea and two episodes of non-bilious emesis.
clinical_rationale: Severe pain requiring IV analgesia, CT KUB diagnostic imaging, and IV antiemetics (multiple resources). Stable hemodynamics place in ESI 3 urgent care.

name: Meera Gupta
chief_complaint: Accidental cookie ingestion, massive lip/tongue angioedema, diffuse hives, wheeze
hpi_narrative: 8-year-old female ingested bakery item 15 mins ago. Mother administered 1 EpiPen prior to arrival. Significant swelling of lips and uvula. Hoarse voice and inspiratory wheezing.
case_type: Pediatric Severe Anaphylaxis with Impending Airway Compromise
clinical_rationale: Severe multisystem anaphylaxis with rapid airway swelling and respiratory compromise. Immediate second dose of Epinephrine, nebulized albuterol, and intubation preparedness (ESI 1).

name: Arjun Patel
chief_complaint: Fall on outstretched hand, visible dinner-fork deformity of right forearm
hpi_narrative: 29-year-old fell while rollerblading. Severe right distal wrist deformity. Radial pulse palpable, capillary refill < 2s, sensation intact to all 5 digits.
clinical_rationale: Severe localized deformity and pain requiring X-rays, procedural sedation/hematoma block, and orthopedic reduction/casting (multiple resources). ESI 3.

name: Harish Bansal
chief_complaint: Progressive fatigue, poor oral intake for 4 days, sunken eyes, dry mucous membranes
hpi_narrative: 84-year-old frail male with severe dehydration. Caregiver reports diminished urine output. Orthostatic dizziness on standing. Borderline renal failure risk.
clinical_rationale: Complex geriatric patient with multiple comorbidities requiring lab workup (electrolytes, creatinine), cautious IV fluid resuscitation, and medication review. ESI 3.
